2M.8 Praise and exalt the name of God with song.

precepts.text: I will bring my people again from Bashan and the depths of the sea, that thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies and the tongue of thy dogs in the same. They have seen thy goings, my King, in the sanctuary: singers before, players on instruments after, damsels with timbrels, beautiful songs, not like the churches. Little Benjamin with their ruler, almost wiped out and the baby tribe; the princes of Judah and their council, Zebulun, and Naphtali, the re-established kingdom. Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents; rebuke the spearmen and the bulls, the powers of the nations, till every one submit himself with pieces of silver, tribute; scatter thou the people that delight in war, the white man, who renamed the Department of Defense the Department of War.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
“The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.” Why bring them again? Because God's people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.” Damn! Our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies, and those nations that run their mouths against us, the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” That is the sanctuary. “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.” People singing before the Lord, not like these churches: beautiful songs, with men and women behind them playing instruments and young girls with timbrels. “Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” Little Benjamin because they almost got wiped out, and they are the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. This is his re-established kingdom.

“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute. “Rebuke the company of spearmen”, the soldiers, “the multitude of the bulls”, the people that have power in the other nations, “with the calves of the people”, their little ones, “till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute. Then, “scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is? The white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War. They delight in war.

This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20: the temple standing, the tribes gathered, the kings bringing tribute, and the fierce nations subdued.

precepts.text: The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; the power of the name is from Him.
precepts.point: The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; He is the power source. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare.
precepts.why:
“O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.” The God of Israel is the power source; strength and power come from Him.

That is the power in the name. “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.” Israel means a prince that has power with God. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare.

precepts.text: He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death, not to the idols of Egypt.
precepts.point: In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. Unto God the Lord belong the issues from death; the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death.
precepts.why:
“at midnight the Lord smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.” Even the prisoners' firstborn died, and Pharaoh's own son died. From the throne to the dungeon, nothing in Egypt stood between the Lord and any firstborn.

In this Christ showed that Osiris and Isis, the supposed Egyptian gods of life and death, control neither life nor death. “He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death.” The issues from death belong to the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not to the idols of Egypt. He is the God of salvation, and he alone brings forth death; that midnight in Egypt, life and death were in his hand and no one else's.

precepts.text: The Lord gave the word; great was the company of those that published it. Moses published what the Lord commanded.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.” Moses wrote the goings out of Israel by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and Moses published it.

So the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls. The word came from the Lord, and Moses was of the company that published what God commanded him to write.

precepts.text: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; as smoke is driven away, as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
precepts.point: The Most High was fighting Israel's battles and winning the wars. It was not because Israel was a great nation of itself that the other nations were defeated; it was because God was with them, the God that brought them out of Egypt and multiplied them into a great nation.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
Every time the ark set forward Moses said, “Rise up, Lord, and let thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.” David sang the same words: “Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.”

David goes on: “As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.” The enemies were scattered at the presence of God, not at the presence of Israel.

The Most High was fighting Israel's battles and winning the wars. It was not because Israel was a great nation of itself that the other nations were defeated; it was because God was with them, the God that brought them out of Egypt and multiplied them into a great nation. The ark went before them to search out a resting place, the cloud of the Lord was upon them by day, and when the ark rested Moses said, “Return, O Lord, unto the many thousands of Israel.”

precepts.text: Hearken diligently and the blessings overtake thee as a nation; the Most High causes thine enemies to be smitten before thy face, coming out one way and fleeing seven ways.
precepts.point: This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing.
precepts.why:
“Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.” This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee”.

Among those blessings: “The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.” Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing. As smoke is driven away and wax melts before the fire, so the wicked perish at the presence of God, and they that hate him flee before him.

precepts.text: Ye shall chase your enemies and they shall fall before you by the sword; five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight.
precepts.point: This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing.
precepts.why:
“And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword. And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.” Five chase a hundred, and a hundred put ten thousand to flight. That is the enemies scattered and those that hate him fleeing before him, as David cries for in Psalm 68.

It is a national blessing, like Deuteronomy 28, not an individual one. When we keep the commandments as a nation, the Most High arises and our enemies fall before us by the sword.

precepts.text: We have a more sure word of prophecy; no prophecy of scripture is of any private interpretation, for holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.
precepts.point: Kings of armies did flee, and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though they lay among the pots, yet shall they be as the wings of a dove covered with silver.
precepts.why:
“The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.” That is why you have different books of people that the Lord spoke to: Ezekiel, Jeremiah and all the prophets in the company of Israel that published what God said. Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” The company that published the word did not speak from their own will or private interpretation; the Lord gave the word, and holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

precepts.text: See now that I, even I, am He, and there is no God with me; I kill and I make alive, I wound and I heal, neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.
precepts.point: There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time you are not going, and when it is your time you are not staying.
precepts.why:
“He that is our God is the God of salvation; and unto God the Lord belong the issues from death.” There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. “See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.”

That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time, you are not going; and when it is your time, you are not staying. He kills and he makes alive, he wounds and he heals, and none can deliver out of his hand. Blessed be the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits; as Lamentations 3 says, his mercy is renewed every morning.

precepts.text: These are the names of the children of Israel which came into Egypt with Jacob: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
precepts.point: There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. These are the tribes of Israel, the sons of Jacob whose name was changed to Israel.
precepts.why:
“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” These are the tribes of Israel, the sons of Jacob, whose name was changed to Israel. “Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob. Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin, Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.”

Benjamin, Judah, Zebulun and Naphtali in the psalm are these same sons who came into Egypt with Jacob. Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel: the congregations are these tribes, with the singers before and the players on instruments after, and the damsels playing with timbrels among them like a marching band.

note.label: Know Your Enemy: God's Foes & Ours

points: The cry is for the Most High to arise so His enemies are scattered and those that hate Him flee before Him.

This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing.
As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

Let the righteous, those keeping the commandments, be glad and rejoice exceedingly before God. We are going to rejoice on our feast days, not oppressed by the enemy, serving the Lord without fear in the Kingdom.
Sing praises to His name, extol Him that rideth upon the heavens by His name Yah, and rejoice before Him. The Lord has many titles as you read the scriptures.
He is a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows; He sets the solitary in families and brings out those bound with chains, but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
Just as when we came out of Egypt, the Most High went before us in the wilderness and in the chariot; He always went before us.
When the Most High went forth before His people and marched through the wilderness, the earth shook and the heavens dropped at His presence, and even Sinai itself was moved.

The scriptures talk about how when the Most High comes, the hailstorms come, the mountains tremble, and thunder and lightning appear. We serve the only true God, the God of Israel, the God of everybody.
He sent a plentiful rain to confirm His inheritance when it was weary, and prepared of His goodness for the poor.

The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it. That is why you have different books of people that the Lord spoke to: Ezekiel, Jeremiah, and all the prophets in the company of Israel that published what God said.
Kings of armies did flee, and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though they lay among the pots, yet shall they be as the wings of a dove covered with silver.
The hill of Bashan is a high hill, but this is the hill which God desired to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it forever. The Most High dwells in Zion, in Jerusalem.
That is why Christ said a city on a hill cannot be hidden; that is the city Jerusalem where the Lord dwells.
The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels, the Lord among them as in Sinai. That is why in Isaiah 66:15 He is coming back with the whirlwind.
He has ascended on high, led captivity captive, and received gifts for men, even for the rebellious, that the Lord God might dwell among them.
Blessed be the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. As it says in Lamentations 3, His mercy is renewed every morning.
He that is our God is the God of salvation, and unto God the Lord belong the issues of death.

There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time you are not going, and when it is your time you are not staying.
The Lord said He will bring His people again from Bashan and from the depths of the sea, that thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies.

The Lord said we are going to walk in the blood of our enemies, because the Lord is a man of war. Israel really does not know war in the sense we are in now; the scriptures talk about how the Lord is going to teach us to know war again.

They have seen the goings of the Most High, the goings of my God my king in the sanctuary. The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after, and among them were the damsels playing with timbrels, like a marching band with women playing instruments.
Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord from the fountain of Israel.

There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. These are the tribes of Israel, the sons of Jacob whose name was changed to Israel.
Thy God hath commanded thy strength; strengthen, O God, that which Thou hast wrought for us because of Thy temple at Jerusalem, and kings shall bring presents unto thee.

Rebuke the company of the spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, till everyone submit himself with pieces of silver; scatter the people that delight in war. Until they submit, paying taxes to us, we are going to make them submit and pay tribute.
Princes shall come out of Egypt, and Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God.
Sing unto God ye kingdoms of the earth, to Him that rideth upon the heavens, who sends out His voice, and that a mighty voice.
Ascribe strength unto God; His excellency is over Israel and His strength is in the clouds. The God of Israel gives strength and power unto His people. Blessed be God.
